I want something that creates impact and income without demanding every hour of my day. My standards for a business are high. Not because I’m looking for an easy way out, but because I’ve seen what happens when people choose the wrong model. I’ve watched brilliant founders burn out, chained to their laptops, wishing for an escape. The business you build will influence your health, your relationships, your freedom… almost everything. I’d rather build the right systems slowly than spend decades wishing I hadn’t settled for a glorified job. Some foundations are simply too important to rush. If you want to learn how to build one that buys back your time, comment 'FieldWork' and I'll send you my guide.
script: Hook with a common misconception about your work ethic.
Correct it by defining the *kind* of business you actually want.
State that your standards for a business are high.
Justify those standards by showing the negative outcome of the alternative (burnout).
Raise the stakes by listing all the life areas a business model affects.
Conclude with a principle about building correctly over building fast.
End with a clear 'Comment KEYWORD' call to action.

ideas.title: I'm okay without a bigger team, and I think that makes some founders uncomfortable.
ideas.headline: I Am Okay Without More
ideas.angle: Frame this as a quiet observation, not an attack. You've noticed that your choice to prioritize life over endless business growth is a foreign concept to many, and you want to speak to the others who feel the same way about choosing 'enough'.
hooks: I'm okay without a bigger team, and I think that makes some founders uncomfortable.
My business doesn't need to grow every quarter, and that seems to be an unpopular opinion.
I'm happy with 'enough', and I've noticed that word makes a lot of entrepreneurs angry.
I don't want to build a billion dollar company, and I think that's hard for some people to hear.
I build my business so I can be offline more, not online more. And that confuses people.
talking_points: I’m okay with enough. And I’ve noticed that simple idea makes a lot of people in the online business world really uncomfortable.
They see a business that’s profitable, that runs smoothly, and the first question is always 'So, what’s next? How do you scale it?'
The expectation is always more. More team members, more revenue, more complexity, more market share.
And when you say, 'I'm good. This is enough. This funds the life I want to live,' you can see the confusion in their eyes.
I think it’s because it holds up a mirror to the hustle they've been sold. The idea that you must always be climbing.
But the whole point of building an online business, for me, was to get my time back. To build it so I could live my life offline.
It was never about building a prison of my own making, no matter how profitable it was.
The goal is not just to build an engine. It is to build an engine that works for you, so you can get back out into the field.
If that idea resonates with you more than the idea of endless scale, I have something that might help.
Comment the word 'FIELD' below, and I will send you my guide on how to build a business that buys back your time.

ideas.title: You can build a business that doesn't consume you.
ideas.headline: Build a Business, Not a Cage
ideas.angle: Translate the original's fatherhood vs. business conflict into your core message: the founder who is trapped by the business they built for freedom. Position the 'hustle culture' narrative as the villain and your 'Build Online, Live Offline' philosophy as the liberating truth.
hooks: You can build a business that doesn't consume you.
Your business is supposed to fund your life, not become your whole life.
Stop sacrificing your life for the business you built to escape a 9-to-5.
That feeling of guilt when you log off? It's a lie.
Let's be honest, you started this for more freedom, not a 24/7 job.
talking_points: You can and you will build this thing without it costing you your life offline.
You have everything you need right now to build a business that serves you, not the other way around.
I'm filming this right now when I 'should' be prepping for a launch, and part of me feels that pull, that guilt.
It's a painful feeling, knowing you're missing a perfect sunset to answer one more email, or cutting a trip short for a meeting that could have waited.
I know so many of you are in the same spot because I get your messages every single day. You feel trapped.
The hustle culture narrative tells you this is the only way. That you have to sacrifice everything now to win later. It's not true.
You have to keep your eyes on what matters most. The life this business is supposed to afford you, the time with people you love, the moments in the wild.
No one will remember your Q4 revenue. They will remember that you were there, present and accounted for.
This is me showing you I'm here, choosing the offline, because I want to be living proof that you can choose your life over the grind and still build something incredible.
We build these online engines so we can return to the field. If you want to see how we do it, comment 'FIELDWORK' below and I will send you my free guide.
